topic: Studio sample: free products to paid deals

msgs.text: We'll send you our product. Can you post a reel?

explainer.say: A brand sends you a free product and asks for a reel. No money.

explainer.unit: spent by Indian brands on influencers in 2024
explainer.say: Yet Indian brands spent three thousand six hundred crore rupees on influencer marketing in 2024.
So is free stuff a good deal, or a trap? Here's how small creators turn it into paid deals.
We've been there. Saying no feels rude, so you say yes to everything.

explainer.text: **83%** of marketers struggle to find the right creators
explainer.say: Here's the twist. In one report, eighty three percent of marketers said they struggle to find the right talent.

explainer.title: Got it free? Still an ad.
lines: Even if the brand didn't ask.
explainer.say: And in India, a free product still counts. ASCI says label it upfront, even if the brand didn't ask.

explainer.card: A free product doesn't pay **your rent**.
explainer.say: But a free product doesn't pay your rent.
One industry report puts reel rates for creators under ten thousand followers at five hundred to five thousand rupees.

explainer.small: Free stuff is a deal only if it gets you
explainer.say: So free stuff is a good deal only when it gets you proof. Then you ask for money.

lines: 1. Say yes only if you'd buy it

explainer.say: Try this. Say yes only if you'd buy it. Label it and post your best. Then send your results and your rate.
